Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
942 PM EDT Sat Sep 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
We continue to monitor rain moving off toward the south and west 
associated with a Nor'easter located offshore.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) A Nor'easter brings below normal temperatures, breezy
  conditions, and some rain at times through this weekend.

- 2) Warm and calm conditions next week before rainfall chances
  return by late next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A Nor'easter brings below normal temperatures,
breezy conditions, and some rain at times through this weekend.

A powerful Nor'easter continues to circulate offshore. As of 930
PM, a band of rainfall associated with this system is tracking 
off toward the southwest into Southern Maryland and Central 
Virginia. Behind this more focused band there a few showers 
that are lingering further northeast. Showers will continue to 
be possible on and off throughout the night, although there 
should be a tendency for the coverage of showers to decrease 
during the second half of the night. Winds will remain gusty out
of the north to northwest overnight.

As the low center circles back into our area tomorrow, expect
more rain late tomorrow morning through the day Sunday. Chances
will be highest across the northeast part of the fcst area, and
this period has the highest chance for rain to reach as far 
west as the Alleghenies. Northeast Maryland could see up to an
inch of rain through the day Sunday. Wind gusts tomorrow will 
be 20-35 mph and up to 40 mph near the Chesapeake Bay.

While rain chances and wind gusts will likely start declining 
by Monday, cloud cover will likely remain stubbornly in place. 
The current forecast calls for upper 60s and lower 70s, but 
would not be surprised if they are a bit lower if clouds are 
thick. As winds shift more northwesterly, some upslope showers 
or drizzle will be possible in the Alleghenies.
 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Generally warm and benign weather next week before rainfall 
chances return by next weekend.

While rain chances and wind gusts decline on Monday, cloud cover 
remains stubborn, potentially limiting sunshine to start the week. 
Our current forecast calls for upper 60s and lower 70s, but could 
trend a bit cooler if a thicker cloud deck persists. As 
northwesterly wind shifts slightly further west, some upslope 
showers or drizzle will be possible in the Alleghenies.

Continuing into the beginning of next week, an upper level ridge 
advances overhead from the west, building high pressure at the 
surface through Wednesday. Overall, this pattern favors dry and 
gradually warmer conditions with highs in the 70s potentially 
creeping up into the low 80s late next week. One potential caveat 
could be Wednesday night into Thursday as a fast moving Clipper 
system passes by to our north. Given all of the forcing remains to 
the north and moisture return ahead of the system is weak, showers 
and thunderstorm potential appear negligible. The next chance for 
rain looks to be Friday and into next weekend ahead of an 
approaching cold front from Canada.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Off and on light showers are expected overnight, although
coverage of those showers should tend to decrease during the
second half of the night. Additional rain showers move in from
the northeast tomorrow. The main impact will be the gusty N to 
NNW winds gusting 25-30 kt on Sunday. Some brief reductions in 
cigs are possible, but vsby restrictions are not anticipated.

Northeasterly to easterly winds continue to weaken on Tuesday and 
shift southerly by Wednesday. VFR conditions are forecast to prevail 
through the middle of next week, with no precipitation chances.

&&

.MARINE...
Occasional gale force gusts have been observed so far today, but
the gradient remains tight and the latest ECMWF shows another
surge in northerly winds tomorrow. Have extended the Gale
Warning through tomorrow for the waters south of Drum Point
where fetch will be longer and winds likely overperform.
Otherwise, strong SCA conditions are expected through Monday.

Favorable, benign marine conditions expected through the middle of 
next week. Southerly channeling is possible over the open waters of 
the Chesapeake Bay on Wednesday, though still uncertain if those 
winds approach SCA strength.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Water levels appear to have begun to slosh back at the bottom of
the bay with increasing tidal anomalies seen now at Straits
Point and Annapolis. Based on forecast trends from surge models,
this prompted the issuance of a Coastal Flood Warning for St.
Marys County for tonight's and Sunday's high tides. A Coastal
Flood Watch was also issued for Anne Arundel County for Sunday's
high tide. New Coastal Flood Advisory was issued for the City of
Alexandria.
